Layering vessel registration and beneficial ownership across different flags is a classic way to obscure who actually controls a vessel, frustrating attribution and asset seizure after an interdiction. Identity manipulation is the strongest risk signal. MMSI changes let a vessel intermittently masquerade under a different identity, breaking the track history investigators would otherwise use to link a vessel to past smuggling runs, rendezvous points, or known trafficking networks. Because MMSI-change vessels carry the highest High-Risk rate of any indicator, identity manipulation is the single most efficient signal for prioritizing interdiction and inspection resources. 04 Atlantic corridor runs both ways 71% of first-time visits fall in North or South Atlantic zones. Cocaine trafficking is often assumed to run one-way, north from South American production hubs to European and North American markets. East & SE Asia drives 34% of MMSI changes but just 16% of dark activity.
